name: BIS Standards Q&A Assistant (SIH-26107)
description: Thin orchestration shell over the BIS assistant backend. Posts a question to POST /chat and renders the validated answer, its cited sources, the routed intent and whether the assistant abstained. Intent routing, hybrid retrieval, reranking, citation validation and abstention all live in the backend service.
weftCode:
# Project: BIS Standards Q&A Assistant (SIH-26107) - backend shell
# Description: Thin orchestration layer over the BIS assistant backend. Routing,
# hybrid retrieval, reranking, citation validation and abstention all live in the
# FastAPI service; this workflow only carries the request in and renders the
# result out.

design_note = Annotation {
  content: ```
## Why this workflow is thin

An earlier draft re-implemented the whole pipeline inside the graph: intent
routing, a hardcoded catalogue, a hand-written FAQ, local embedding/Qdrant/
reranker servers, and its own citation validator. That version could not run -
and more importantly it duplicated logic that already exists, tested, in the
backend.

Problems it had, kept here so they are not reintroduced:
- Used groq/llama-3.3-70b-versatile and llama-3.1-8b-instant. Groq has retired
  the Llama chat models; both 404. Only the prompt-guard variants remain.
- Required local servers on :8080 (embeddings), :6333 (Qdrant) and :8081
  (reranker). The project runs entirely on hosted APIs now.
- Shipped 6 sample standards standing in for 6,209, two with wrong committees
  (IS 13252 is LITD 7 not LITD 10; IS 9873 is PCD 30 not PCD 12). Hardcoded
  incorrect regulatory metadata is exactly what the citation validator exists
  to prevent, and it sails straight through - the validator checks that a
  marker resolves to a source, not that the source is true.
- Cited a hand-written FAQ blob as [S1] against a bare bis.gov.in URL. That is
  a citation that looks authoritative and is untraceable to any document.

One HTTP call replaces all of it. Correctness has a single home.

## Configuration
Point the "BIS Backend" node at your API. Local: http://localhost:8000/chat
The endpoint returns answer, sources, abstained, intent, latency_ms and
structured, matching docs/FRONTEND_PROMPT.md.
  ```
}

# ---- Trigger ----
question_trigger = ApiPost -> (question: String) {
  label: "User Question (POST)"
}

language_choice = Text {
  label: "Language"
  value: "auto"
}

# ---- Request ----
request_body = ExecPython(question: String, language: String) -> (body: JsonDict) {
  label: "Build Request"
  code: ```
q = (question or "").strip()
if not q:
    raise ValueError("question is required")
return {"body": {"message": q, "session_id": None, "language": language or "auto"}}
  ```
}
request_body.question = question_trigger.question
request_body.language = language_choice.value

backend = Http {
  label: "BIS Backend (POST /chat)"
  url: "http://localhost:8000/chat"
  method: "POST"
}
backend.body = request_body.body

# ---- Response ----
parse = ExecPython(response: String) -> (answer: String, sources: JsonDict, abstained: Boolean, intent: String, notes: String) {
  label: "Parse Response"
  code: ```
import json

# A transport failure must not surface as a confident answer. If the body is
# not the JSON we expect, report that plainly and mark it abstained so the
# caller treats it as "no answer", not as a result.
try:
    r = json.loads(response) if isinstance(response, str) else (response or {})
except Exception:
    r = {}

if not isinstance(r, dict) or "answer" not in r:
    return {
        "answer": "The assistant backend did not return a usable response. Check that the service is running and reachable.",
        "sources": {},
        "abstained": True,
        "intent": "error",
        "notes": "unparseable backend response",
    }

# Sources arrive as a list of {marker, title, url, locator, is_number,
# doc_type}. Re-key by marker so [S1] in the text maps straight to its card.
sources = {}
for s in (r.get("sources") or []):
    if isinstance(s, dict) and s.get("marker"):
        sources[s["marker"]] = s

notes = []
if r.get("abstained"):
    notes.append("abstained: evidence was too weak to answer")
for w in (r.get("warnings") or []):
    notes.append(str(w))

return {
    "answer": r.get("answer") or "",
    "sources": sources,
    "abstained": bool(r.get("abstained")),
    "intent": str(r.get("intent") or ""),
    "notes": "; ".join(notes),
}
  ```
}
parse.response = backend.body

# ---- Outputs ----
out_answer = Debug { label: "Answer" }
out_answer.data = parse.answer

out_sources = Debug { label: "Cited Sources" }
out_sources.data = parse.sources

out_abstained = Debug { label: "Abstained?" }
out_abstained.data = parse.abstained

out_intent = Debug { label: "Intent" }
out_intent.data = parse.intent

out_notes = Debug { label: "Notes / Warnings" }
out_notes.data = parse.notes
